title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this part of the 'équation des lacets' manuscript, Grothendieck attaches to a pair of 2×2 matrices (ρ, σ) a group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over a base S. The 'modular case' is singled out at the end of this page.

Ingredients, as far as they can be read from this and the neighbouring pages:
- T_ρ and T_σ are the commutative group schemes (tori) of units of the algebras O_S[ρ] and O_S[σ], i.e. the centralizers of ρ and σ in GL_2.
- ST_ρ and ST_σ are their determinant-one subgroups.
- τ_{ρ,σ} is a 'toric' group with neutral component T_ρ ×_{G_m} T_σ.
- M_{ρ,σ}(0) is the 'toric part' of M_{ρ,σ}, mapping onto τ_{ρ,σ}.
- 𝔖^+_{ρ,σ} ≅ SG is an SL_2-like piece. One has M = M(0)·𝔖^+, a semidirect product.
- There are canonical characters χ: M → G_m and ε_2, ε_3: M → μ_2, and M° is the neutral component, with M/M° ≅ μ_2×μ_2.

The page computes some canonical subgroups and lower bounds for centres.

(46) M^{°+} := Ker(χ, ε_2, ε_3) ≅ ST_ρ × ST_σ × 𝔖^+_{ρ,σ}. The product is direct because ST_ρ × ST_σ is central in M°, as stated on the previous page.

(47) Centre(M°) ⊃ ST_ρ × ST_σ × μ_2. Here ST_ρ × ST_σ sits in M(0)° and μ_2 is the centre {±1} of SG ≅ 𝔖^+.

(48) Hence there is a subgroup μ_2×μ_2×μ_2 ⊂ 1×ST_ρ×ST_σ×μ_2, using ±1 ∈ ST_ρ and ±1 ∈ ST_σ. This subgroup is in fact central in all of M.

(49) More precisely, Centre(M) ⊃ 1 × S'T_ρ × μ_2 × μ_2, where:
- (50) S'T_ρ = {g ∈ T_ρ : (det g)² = 1};
- (51) there is an exact sequence 1 → ST_ρ → S'T_ρ → μ_2 → 1, the last map being ε_3 = det.

On the σ-side only μ_2 survives. The non-neutral component (the ε_2 part, the 'complex conjugation' τ_∞ of the next page) acts nontrivially on T_σ.

(52) Intersecting with M° (where ε_3 = 1) gives Centre(M) ∩ M° ⊃ 1 × ST_ρ × μ_2 × μ_2. The four factors sit inside T_0, T_ρ, T_σ and 𝔖^+ respectively.

(53) Modular case: det ρ = 1 (equivalently det σ = 1, equivalently a parameter ν = −1). Then ρ = [[0,1],[−1,1]] and σ = [[0,1],[−1,0]].
- Equivalent conditions: σ² = −1; ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0; or the images in PGL satisfy σ̃² = ρ̃³ = 1.
- These are the standard generators of SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 (indeed ρ³ = −1 = σ²).
- In this case ρ ∈ ST_ρ and σ ∈ ST_σ, so both are central in M°.
- The next page then gets a homomorphism Z/6 × Z/4 → Centre(M°), (i, j) ↦ i_ρ(ρ^i) i_σ(σ^j). It is a monomorphism when 2 is invertible on S.
- Over Z, M_{ρ,σ}(Z) ≅ (Z/6 × D_4) ⋉ SL(2,Z).

Purpose. The page computes the centre and canonical subgroups of the group scheme M_{ρ,σ}, which deforms or interpolates the arithmetic of the modular group. This feeds into the study of the loop (lacets) relations, i.e. GT-type relations. The margin note says the whole page should be redone 'modulo radicaux', i.e. after passing to the reductive quotient.
errors: (46) is written as a direct product. This requires the centrality of ST_ρ×ST_σ in M^{°+}; that is asserted on the previous page but not proved here.

The centre computations (47), (49), (52) are only inclusions (⊃), not equalities. The margin note itself warns that one should be careful about identifying them as equalities, especially modulo radicals.
On the next page, 'l'hom (53) est un mono' should refer to (54).
The reason only μ_2 of T_σ (rather than S'T_σ) is central in M is not spelled out. It presumably comes from the action of the ε_2-component (τ_∞) on T_σ.

ideas.what: Group scheme M_{ρ,σ} over a base, built from the tori T_ρ, T_σ and an SL_2-like part, generalizing the amalgam structure of SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6
ideas.modern_name: group schemes attached to pairs of elliptic elements / families of 'modular-like' groups

ideas.what: Lower bounds for the centre of M and M°, the subgroup S'T_ρ = {(det g)² = 1}, and the exact sequence 1→ST→S'T→μ_2→1
ideas.modern_name: centre computation of a non-connected group scheme

ideas.what: Characterization of the modular case via det ρ = 1, σ² = −1, ρ² − ρ + 1 = 0
ideas.modern_name: standard elliptic generators of SL(2,Z) of orders 4 and 6

missed.claim: Grothendieck flags that the whole centre computation should be redone 'modulo radicaux' (in the reductive quotient) and that some inclusions should be equalities. This refinement is not carried out on this page.
missed.quote: Toute la page devrait être reprise (au moins) dans le contexte "modulo radicaux"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor technical loose end within an unpublished framework of group schemes M_{ρ,σ}. The framework as a whole (deformations of the modular group as group schemes over Z) is little known, but this page is routine bookkeeping within it.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine centre computations inside an unpublished framework. The framework itself (the group schemes M_{ρ,σ}) is mildly interesting, but this page adds only bookkeeping.
transcription_corrections: (48) is better read as 'μ_2×μ_2×μ_2 ⊂ 1×ST_ρ×ST_σ×μ_2' (an inclusion sign, not 'd[?]').
In (52), the label under the first factor is T_0, not attached to ST_ρ. The labels T_0, T_ρ, T_σ, 𝔖^+ sit under the factors 1, ST_ρ, μ_2, μ_2 respectively.
The archive page number is 419 (handwritten at bottom left).
Margin of (46)–(47): 'Toute la page devrait être reprise (au moins) dans le contexte "modulo radicaux" ; "attention" à la tentation [?] d'identifier [?] par une égalité, cf plus loin...'.
The margin marks next to (49) and (52) look like 'id' / '?'.
